not_supported_as_scientific_claims: EIA reduces provider-metered model input by 95.8%.
EIA improves outcome quality based on this single paired evaluation.
EIA improves resilience in this run.
Nine reusable agents imply quantified financial benefit.
The source label 'Trust Improvement Observed' is itself independent causal proof of trust improvement.
paper_usage_rule: Use this record as observational/runtime evidence and as a paired feasibility case. Do not use it as a causal treatment-effect estimate until the frozen sample floors, quality/evidence floors, and required approvals are satisfied.

supported_observations.claim: The workload contract records the same runtime profile, agent, system, service, entity set, reasoning mode, prompt, top value, date range, and filters across the baseline and EIA arms.
Both the direct baseline and EIA arm completed with SUCCESS and recorded six findings and zero actions.
The report records outcome-quality parity at 70.0/100 versus 70.0/100 for this paired evaluation.

supported_observations.basis: transparent 4-bytes-per-token estimates, not provider billing/input telemetry
supported_observations.claim: The direct baseline is reported at approximately 9,895 estimated raw-context tokens, while the EIA compact context is reported at approximately 408 estimated tokens.
EIA preserved 100 unique records, removed zero duplicates, reported zero conflicts, and recorded evidence coverage of four categories/items: two authoritative and two supporting.
The run recorded 8,450.429 ms of synchronous EIA microkernel overhead.
End-to-end latency, SAP wait, MCP wait, RAG/vector wait, and LLM time were not measured for this evaluation.
The release identified nine agents potentially affected by a shared admission/evidence contract, without financially proving reuse value.
The source evaluation explicitly blocks customer/optimization claims because the 30 functional-pair and 100 latency-pair floors are not met and named approval is still required.
